name: diff-viewer-git

nondeterminism.reason: It renders the WORKING TREE's own `git diff`, so the golden is a snapshot of whatever was uncommitted in the corpus directory when it was captured — and it drifts on every unrelated edit to any file, on every commit, and on every branch. Not machine-specific in the usual sense: machine-INDEPENDENT of the hardware and entirely dependent on the source tree, which is the worst possible property for a golden, because the tree changes constantly during the very work the gate exists to police. Observed directly: it drifted during a `verify` run that overlapped edits to two files in this same directory, and passed again once the tree settled.
nondeterminism.varying_region: The file list and the hunk bodies, i.e. every row the diff viewer paints — there is no stable subset to point at. Its own notes already called this out before Phase 0; the four-render proof is what turned the prediction into a measurement.
nondeterminism.surface_of_fix: Give the scenario a fixture: point the viewer at a seeded diff from a temp file (or an env-selected diff source) instead of the live repository. Until then the text assertions still cover it — only the golden is withheld. Note diff-viewer-turn, which reaches the SAME renderer through /changes, IS goldened: it renders a stored turn diff from the mock agent script, which is static.

notes: The git-diff mode of the viewer: file list left, hunk detail right, with +/- counts in the header. Strongly ENV-dependent (it renders the working tree's own diff), so this baseline is machine-specific by construction — pin the repo state or keep it advisory. Catches the pane split and the add/delete colour coding, which is pure style-baseline territory. The third needle was 'Files'; the header renders 'N files' (lowercase), so it was mis-cased and could never match.
